items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: Well, you see, years ago, the Masons used to use music at every funeral.

ctx.x: Well, you see, years ago, the Masons used to use music at every funeral. But I don't know, in the later years, these men that come into these things, they kind of abolish that. But that's in the Constitution. Every Mason is supposed to be buried with a band of music. But these fellas get away from it, some kind of way, I don't know. See what I mean? Some of them say the bands is too high and all that. The bands are not too high because they're not paying much of members pay for it.

So what about a Mason who's a Catholic? Can he... No, Masons can't be Catholics. No, Catholics can't be Masons. Are you sure? I'm pretty sure. Is that right? That's what I hear. Yeah, that's what I've always heard and I'm sure. Yeah, but I've seen it happen here. Maybe. I've seen it happen in New Orleans. Yeah. It could be. That's why I'm asking. Because I can point out something to you later. Okay.
